title: Child Routes & Lazy Loading 🧩
description: Create nested views with child routes and optimise performance with lazy loading.

slides.title: Child Routes: Nested Views 🪆
slides.content:
# Hierarchical Routing

Often a component has its own sub‑pages. For example, a `DashboardComponent` might have sections like `stats` and `settings`.

Define a `children` array in the route:
```typescript
{
  path: 'dashboard',
  component: DashboardComponent,
  children: [
    { path: 'stats', component: StatsComponent },
    { path: 'settings', component: SettingsComponent }
  ]
}
```

The child components will be rendered into a `<router-outlet>` inside the parent’s template.

slides.title: Child Route Example
slides.content: Parent template must contain its own `<router-outlet>`:

quizData.question: Child routes are rendered into the same `<router-outlet>` as the parent.
quizData.explanation: The parent component must have its own `<router-outlet>` to display child components.

slides.title: Lazy Loading: Load on Demand ⚡
slides.content:
By default, all components are bundled at startup. For large apps, this slows initial load.

**Lazy loading** defers the loading of a feature module until the user navigates to it.

Instead of pointing to a component, the route points to a module using `loadChildren`:
```typescript
{
  path: 'admin',
  loadChildren: () => import('./admin/admin.module').then(m => m.AdminModule)
}
```

Angular generates a separate JS chunk for this module, loaded only when needed.

slides.title: Setting Up a Lazy‑Loaded Module
slides.content:
Step 1: Create a feature module with its own routing.
Step 2: In the root routes, use `loadChildren`.

slides.title: Preloading Strategies 🏎️
slides.content:
Lazy loading improves initial load, but causes a small delay when navigating to a new module for the first time.

Angular offers **preloading strategies** to load lazy modules in the background after the app starts.

* `PreloadAllModules` – preloads every lazy module.
* Custom strategy – selectively preload high‑priority modules.

Set in `forRoot()`:
```typescript
RouterModule.forRoot(routes, { preloadingStrategy: PreloadAllModules })
```

This combines fast startup with instant navigation.

quizData.question: What is the main benefit of lazy loading a module?

options.text: It makes the app run faster after every click.
It reduces the initial bundle size by loading code only when needed.
It makes the router work offline.

quizData.explanation: Lazy loading splits code into chunks, decreasing the initial download size.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Organise by Feature

Create feature modules for each major section (e.g., AdminModule, ShopModule) and lazy‑load them. It makes the codebase maintainable and speeds up development builds.
